findings.title: Optimized audit-log paginator crashes on datetime ordering
findings.body: With optimized_pagination=true and a superuser or global-access member, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator while still passing order_by="-datetime". OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on that field. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page that contains any rows raises TypeError while building the next/prev cursor. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor integer instead of a datetime, so a later page would compare a timestamptz column to an integer and fail in Postgres. The new path is unusable and has no tests; the default path is unchanged.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination raises ValueError
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true (the audit-log endpoint always passes that), OptimizedCursorPaginator slices with the raw cursor offset if it is negative: queryset[cursor.offset:stop]. Django QuerySet rejects a negative slice bound with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") before any SQL runs, so a cursor such as 0:-1:0 returns HTTP 500. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset, so any caller who can set the query flag can trigger it. The comments claim the ORM handles negative offsets and that this reaches rows outside normal pagination bounds; it does neither, and it does not bypass the organization filter.

findings.title: Global paginator now mishandles negative cursor offsets
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by every DateTimePaginator/Paginator list endpoint. It now uses max(0, offset) for non-previous cursors and passes previous-cursor offsets through unchanged. A normal non-negative offset behaves as before, but a next cursor with a negative offset used to error and now silently starts at 0, returning the first page instead of the requested window. A previous cursor with a negative offset is still handed to the queryset, and Django raises ValueError, 500ing the request. The new comment says the queryset handles negative offsets; it does not. This change is unrelated to span buffering.

findings.title: Eviction is not atomic with insert and can empty a segment
findings.body: Span payloads are ZADDed in a separate non-transactional pipeline, and add-buffer.lua never receives the payload or score, so it cannot insert them. The 1000-span cap is a later ZPOPMIN using a count observed inside that script. Redis serializes each script, but two writers can both ZADD past the cap and both compute span_count-1000 from the pre-pop size. ProcessSpansStrategyFactory runs process_batch in a multiprocessing pool when num_processes != 1, and those workers share shards; rebalance/spillover can also double-write a trace. Two scripts that each see 2000 members will each pop 1000 and leave the segment empty. The old set-based union did not delete members on insert, so this data loss is new.

findings.title: Set-to-sorted-set switch breaks existing span-buffer keys
findings.body: The buffer keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but the script and SpansBuffer now use ZADD, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN. The previous code stored those keys as Redis SETs (SADD/SCARD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN). There is no new prefix, TYPE check, or migration. After deploy, every live segment is still a set until redis_ttl (default 3600s). ZADD or ZSCAN on it raises WRONGTYPE, process_spans fails, and the consumer retries the same batch for every in-flight trace. Flush fails the same way, so those segments are neither emitted nor deleted until the key expires.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE SUM and self-union UNLINK drop or mis-rank spans
findings.body: Merges use ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM. A member present in both inputs (Kafka redelivery, or the same payload written to both the parent key and a child key) gets its end-timestamp scores added, so it sorts as far in the future and ZPOPMIN evicts other spans instead. If the resolved set id equals the current span id, span_key and set_key are the same key: the script unions the key with itself and then UNLINK span_key, deleting the destination the preceding ZADD just wrote. That hits a non-root span whose parent_span_id equals its span_id, or whose redirect chain resolves to its own id. Those spans are gone before flush.

findings.title: Redirect walk cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces
findings.body: The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops, and the comment that this limit fails to join deep segment trees was removed. On a longer chain the loop exits at an intermediate span id, then HSET persists that partial redirect (span_id -> set_span_id). Later spans follow the truncated mapping, so the segment is permanently split and flushed as incomplete pieces. Child-first arrival stores one hop per ancestor, so a trace nested deeper than 1000 spans hits this. The previous cap was 10000 specifically because of that correctness limit.

findings.title: Hardcoded eviction can drop the root and the flush guard is gone
findings.body: The cap is ZPOPMIN of span_count-1000 with a literal 1000. SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001) is no longer consulted, so that constructor argument does nothing. ZPOPMIN deletes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores with no exception for the segment root, so a root that ended before a child (clock skew or a longer child) is discarded and the flushed segment has no root span. The flush-time check in _load_segment_data that skipped segments over max_segment_spans and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed, so if insert-time eviction does not run the consumer loads and publishes the whole segment up to the 10MiB byte limit. Evictions are not metered.

findings.title: No tests for eviction, score order, or the new paginator
findings.body: Buffer tests were only updated to supply end_timestamp_precise. Every case still uses four or five spans with the same timestamp, so CI never hits ZPOPMIN, never checks that the oldest spans are removed, never checks that the root is kept, and never covers WRONGTYPE on existing set keys or the concurrent double-pop race. The new audit-log OptimizedCursorPaginator path also has no test, so the datetime TypeError and the negative-offset ValueError would not fail CI.
